An inequality is like an equation, but with less than, greater than, or the or equal to versions. And there's one big rule: flip the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.
The SAT loves trap words. At least means greater than or equal to. At most and no more than mean less than or equal to. More than means greater than. Fewer than means less than.
Think of at least sixteen years old to drive. That means sixteen or more. Sixteen counts.
You must be at least sixteen to drive. So a is greater than or equal to sixteen. If you wrote a is greater than sixteen, a sixteen year old couldn't drive.
Now the flip. Negative two x is greater than eight. Divide both sides by negative two. Because you divided by a negative, flip the sign. x is less than negative four.
Trap alert. If you forgot to flip, test a point. Zero: is negative two times zero greater than eight? No. So x greater than negative four is wrong.
Testing a point works on graphs too. Is the point one, four a solution of y greater than two x plus one? Plug in. Two times one plus one is three. Four is greater than three. Yes.
Let's try an SAT style question. In twelve x plus nineteen y is less than or equal to three hundred, what does nineteen y mean?
Nineteen is the cost of one y item, and y is how many. So nineteen y is the total spent on y items, in dollars.
Trap alert. Nineteen y is not the number of y items. That's just y. Nineteen y is money.
Your turn. Pause the video. Solve negative three x is less than or equal to twelve.
Divide by negative three and flip. x is greater than or equal to negative four.
Remember three things. At least means greater than or equal to. At most means less than or equal to. And flip the sign when you divide by a negative. Great work.
